# Navakanipāta (AN 9)

**ID:** AN 9
**Section:** Aṅguttaranikāya (an)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Navakanipāta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Navakanipāta* ("The Book of the Nines") is the ninth major division (*nipāta*) of the *Aṅguttaranikāya*, organizing discourses around numerical sets and doctrines categorized under nine items. Key doctrinal themes running through the collection include the progressive nine meditative attainments (*samāpatti*) culminating in the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodha*), featured prominently in AN 9.31, the *Jhānasutta* (AN 9.36), and AN 9.41 [Anālayo 2014; Kuznetsova et al. 2012; Shulman 2014]. Other discourses address the ending of the concatenation of karma (*kammanidānasaṅkhaya*) through the eradication of greed, aversion, and delusion (AN 9.13) [IABU 2012], bodily contemplation to overcome lust in the *Gaṇḍasutta* (AN 9.15) [McMahan 2008], the role of the four *satipaṭṭhāna*s in abandoning the five hindrances (AN 9.64) [Wen 2011], and the karmic value of giving (*dāna*) in the *Velāmasutta* (AN 9.20) [Wen 2011]. Disciplinary matters, such as the suspension of the *uposatha*, also find parallels in Vinaya traditions [Lueritthikul 2015].

**Sources**

- [Anālayo 2014] Bhikkhu Anālayo, The Dawn of Abhidharma (2014) — Discussion of the nine progressive meditative attainments in AN 9.41.
- [IABU 2012] Proceedings of the 2nd IABU Conference: Buddhist Philosophy and Meditation Practice (2012) — Analysis of AN 9.13 regarding karma, brahmacariya, and the destruction of defilements.
- [Lueritthikul 2015] Phra Weerachai Lueritthikul, Diplomatic Edition and Comparative Study of the Posadhasthapanavastu of Mulasarvastivada Vinaya (2015) — Mention of the Uposatha discourse in the Navakanipāta compared to Vinaya texts.
- [Kuznetsova et al. 2012] Irina Kuznetsova, Jonardon Ganeri, Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, Hindu and Buddhist Ideas in Dialogue: Self and No-Self (2012) — Discussion of the Jhāna Sutta (AN 9.36) and formless meditative attainments.
- [McMahan 2008] David L. McMahan, The Making of Buddhist Modernism (2008) — Citation of AN 9.15 regarding the contemplation of the foulness of the body.
- [Shulman 2014] Eviatar Shulman, Rethinking the Buddha: Early Buddhist Philosophy as Meditative Perception (2014) — Discussion of AN 9.31 and saññāvedayitanirodha.
- [Wen 2011] Tzungkuen Wen, A Study of Sukkhavipassaka in Pāli Buddhism (2011) — Citations of AN 9.64 on satipaṭṭhāna and AN 9.20 on gifts and karma compared to Chinese parallel.
